notes: Fixed port kinds: Grove cable ends are now 'wire-end' (plugs) and every Grove socket on the modules, carrier and hub is a 'header-socket', so each cable join is a compatible wire-end into header-socket pair. The MKR Zero's USB receptacle is also a header-socket.

The Grove I2C Hub, Grove cable, and each Grove module are new part types; a Grove 4-pin connector is modelled as one bundled port (GROVE / A0 / D0 / D1 / TWI), so VCC/GND/signal lines are not separated. The TWI (SDA+SCL) pair is likewise bundled as one 'TWI' port on the MKR Zero and the carrier.
The catalogue grove-relay-module has separate VCC/GND/SIG ports; the Grove cable is attached to its SIG port to stand for the Grove connector.
The Arduino MKR Zero is a new type (not in the catalogue). It plugs onto the MKR Connector Carrier via its headers; only the pins used (A0, D0, D1, TWI, VIN, GND) are modelled.
The manual's BOM lists a Grove DPS310 barometric sensor and OLED connected via the I2C hub on the TWI port; the hub's third output is unused.

The 'next step' power diagram is not available as text; the relay is assumed wired as: 12V supply + -> carrier VIN screw terminal -> relay COM; relay NO -> pump; pump other terminal -> GND. The 12V supply is also assumed to power the board through the carrier's VIN/GND screw block.

Two solid wires of different lengths (about 10 cm difference) are soldered to two non-adjacent (not internally connected) tinned bars of the water sensor; the other ends are placed in the tank. They are modelled as jumper-wire parts; the solder itself is recorded as the 'solder' join method rather than a part. The tank, plant vase and USB host are not modelled.
The pump/valve is modelled as a dc-motor. The USB cable is modelled port-less and connected to the MKR Zero's USB port; its host end is not specified.
